_what_this_is: Transit days per supplier — dispatch to arrival at the planning node.
Read only where a purchase extract carries a confirmed-delivery or dispatch date
and no goods receipt. There the lead-time clock can be measured as far as the
supplier's dispatch and no further, so the transit leg is stated here and added:
An extract that carries a goods receipt does not use this file at all. A measured
order-to-arrival lead time is better than a measured order-to-dispatch one plus a
number from a config file, and the receipt path stays the default wherever the
_why_there_is_no_default: A supplier absent from this table gets no lead time from this path — the item
falls through to the planned delivery time in the item master, labelled as the
stated value it is, and the run reports the count.
The alternative is to treat a missing entry as zero transit, and that is the
expensive direction: a lead time short by the whole transit leg understates the
reorder point, so the order goes out too late and the shortage arrives before the
goods. Set `default_days` if you want one number to stand in for the suppliers
you have not listed; leaving it null means they are reported rather than guessed.
_matching: Keys match on the start of the supplier string, so `SIM001` matches
`SIM001 TYCO ELECTRONICS`. This is the same prefix rule
`supplier_incoterm.json` uses, and it is here because export columns routinely
carry the code and the name in one field. The longest matching key wins, so a
specific plant can override a group.
Where the transit time differs by origin for one supplier, key on whatever the
export actually distinguishes them by — usually a separate vendor code per
shipping plant, which is what SAP's vendor-supplying-plant produces.
_what_it_costs_in_accuracy: A stated transit time is a constant, and a constant has no variance. The lead-time
sigma measured through this path is the variability of the *dispatch* leg only, so
safety stock covers less lead-time risk than it appears to. The run says so, and
`lt_basis` on every output row says which basis produced the number.
